name: Foreign National of Ethiopian Origin ID ("Yellow Card") (Proclamation No. 270/2002)

qualifying_event.description: A 'Foreign National of Ethiopian Origin' includes anyone who was previously an Ethiopian national, or who has at least one parent, grandparent, or great-grandparent who was Ethiopian. This is NOT citizenship -- it exists specifically as a workaround because Ethiopia does not permit dual citizenship, letting members of the diaspora who naturalised elsewhere retain most of the practical benefits of Ethiopian nationality without formally being Ethiopian citizens.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Documentation establishing prior Ethiopian nationality, or the qualifying ancestral link to a parent/grandparent/great-grandparent who held it.

requirements.blocker_text: Previously an Ethiopian national, or has at least one parent, grandparent, or great-grandparent who was Ethiopian, reaching to the third generation.

evidence_required.document: Documentation of prior Ethiopian nationality or the qualifying ancestral link

outcome.duration_length: not confirmed in this build -- the Proclamation defers validity/renewal terms to subordinate regulations not located in this pass

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR-hosted) -- Proclamation No. 270/2002, 'Providing Foreign Nationals of Ethiopian Origin with Certain Rights to be Exercised in their Country of Origin': eligibility (former citizen, or parent/grandparent/great-grandparent was Ethiopian); Art. 5 rights (no visa/residence permit needed, work authorization without a separate permit, pension scheme inclusion, domestic-investor classification exempting from foreign capital thresholds, removal of Civil Code property/service restrictions); Art. 6 exclusions (no right to vote or stand for office, barred from regular defense/security/diplomatic-corps service)

Immigration and Citizenship Service (ICS), Ethiopia -- confirms the card is administered as three distinct services: 'Ethiopian Origin ID,' 'Ethiopian Origin ID by Marriage,' and 'Ethiopian Origin ID for Children (Under 18 Years Old)' -- no eligibility/duration/fee detail beyond category existence

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ethiopia). STATUS: DRAFT -- the substantive eligibility and rights detail is tier-2 UNHCR/Refworld sourced (a verbatim hosting of the primary Proclamation text); a tier-1 ICS page confirms the card is administered as three sub-services but adds no eligibility detail of its own, so the hard requirement cites the tier-2 source and the file stays draft. THIS IS ETHIOPIA'S MARQUEE ROUTE: a near-citizen status reaching THREE GENERATIONS back (parent/grandparent/great-grandparent), explicitly created as the direct consequence of Ethiopia's no-dual-citizenship rule (see et_citizenship_naturalisation.json) -- it is the diaspora's practical alternative to holding actual Ethiopian citizenship alongside a foreign one. Rights granted are extensive: no visa/residence permit ever needed, full work authorization, pension-scheme access, and critically, classification as a DOMESTIC investor -- exempting holders entirely from the USD 50,000-200,000 capital thresholds that apply to ordinary foreign investors (see et_investor_residence.json). Rights explicitly WITHHELD: no vote, no standing for elected office, no regular service in defense/security/diplomatic roles -- a clean, statute-defined near-citizen-but-not-citizen boundary. GAP: the card's validity/renewal period is deferred by the Proclamation to subordinate regulations not located in this build; a commonly-cited '5 years' figure circulates in general commentary but could not be confirmed specifically for this card at tier-1/2, so it is not asserted here. dual_citizenship_allowed is TRUE for this route specifically since it is expressly NOT a citizenship grant -- contrast with every citizenship file in this build, all FALSE.
